title: One Pair of Dumbbells Is Enough for a Full-Body Workout
description: Six exercises, one pair of dumbbells, 35 minutes. A full-body plan for home or a private gym, plus how to progress when you only own one weight.
excerpt: You don't need a rack, a cable machine, or three kinds of barbell. One pair of dumbbells covers the whole body — if you know how to add load without adding kilos.
content:
Most people who start training at home buy one pair of dumbbells and decide a month later that it isn't enough. The problem is almost never the iron.

## Six exercises cover everything

Goblet-style squat with the dumbbells at your shoulders, Romanian deadlift, overhead press, bent-over row, lunges, and push-ups with your hands on the dumbbells. Three rounds, 8–12 reps, 60 seconds rest. That's 35 minutes and there isn't a muscle left without a job. Want more? Add a seventh: a 40-step farmer's walk.

## How to progress with a single weight

Progressive overload isn't only about kilos. Slow the lowering phase to three seconds. Add a one-second pause at the bottom. Cut rest from 90 seconds to 45. Or switch to unilateral versions — a single-leg Romanian deadlift with one dumbbell is far harder than the two-handed version at the same weight. Only once you've run out of these do you actually need heavier equipment.

## When dumbbells stop being enough

Roughly when you can do 15 clean squat reps with your heaviest variation and feel nothing the next day. Legs outgrow dumbbells first; the upper body lasts much longer. That's the point to train somewhere with heavy barbells and a rack once or twice a week, and keep the rest at home.

That's exactly what private gyms are for: book [GymHome](https://gymhome.cz) for a 75-minute block, come alone or with one other person, and use kit you'd never fit at home. And if you're setting up a training corner, [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) takes a photo of the room and shows you where things actually fit.
